newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-CHILD STAR HINGIS SCORES $10 MILLION DEAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CHILD STAR HINGIS SCORES $10 MILLION DEAL.

text.p: Swiss tennis star Martina Hingis has signed a US$10 million deal to promote an Italian sportswear label over four years, making the 16-year-old a mutli-millionaire after only one full season on tour.
Sportswear company Sergio Tacchini announced the deal on Tuesday at the Australian Open, as Hingis swept into the second round of the year's first grand slam in straight sets.

"The Swiss 16-year-old will keep on wearing the historic Italian brand till 2001," the company said in a statement handed to reporters at the Open. It said its "total investment" in the deal would be $10 million but gave no further details.
Hingis, who is tipped to one day succeed German Steffi Graf at the top of women's tennis, shrugged her shoulders when asked later how she felt to be earning so much money.
"I'm allowed to get this money," she replied, adding she did not concern herself too closely with the details of her mounting sponsorship deals, and preferred to keep her mind on the court.
"I know what contracts I've got, but I just don't care. You just play your tennis," she said.
The sportswear deals caps off a lucrative 12 months for the playful tennis star, now ranked four in the world. In 1996, she earned $1.3 million in prize money alone.
